CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

scenarios.name: customer-not-on-file
scenarios.why: customer 5 has generated accounts but no CUSTOMER record: INQCUST NOTFND, 'N'; CUSTOMER-FOUND 'N', COMM-FAIL-CODE '1', NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS 0, no SQL

scenarios.name: customer-zero
scenarios.why: CUSTOMER-NUMBER zero: not looked up (no LINK), CUSTOMER-FOUND 'N', COMM-FAIL-CODE '1', NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS 0

scenarios.name: customer-9999999999
scenarios.why: CUSTOMER-NUMBER 9999999999 (on the CUSTOMER file): not looked up either, 'N' / '1'

scenarios.name: caller-leaves-data
scenarios.why: the caller's COMMAREA arrives with account 1's fields already holding text; every field after the POINTER is overwritten when the customer has accounts

scenarios.name: open-deadlock-abends-ad2z
scenarios.why: #6271 (X73): OPEN ACC-CURSOR deadlocks (-911) and the CICS-Db2 attach's syncpoint rollback fails: the task abends AD2Z, so ABEND-HANDLING takes its AD2Z arm (SQLERRMC the deadlock reason code 00C90088) before the program's own abend path LINKs ABNDPROC

scenarios.name: fetch-deadlock-abends-ad2z
scenarios.why: #6271 (X73): the first FETCH of ACC-CURSOR deadlocks (-911) and the attach's rollback fails: AD2Z, so the arm takes the abend path from inside the FETCH loop (generated rows give customer 1 fewer than two accounts, so the second FETCH of the hand case is not reachable here)

scenarios.name: link-inqcust-abends-afcr
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70): the LINK to INQCUST abends AFCR (RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACCCU's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes it and the callee never runs

scenarios.name: link-inqcust-abends-afcs
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70): the LINK to INQCUST abends AFCS (RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACCCU's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes it and the callee never runs

scenarios.name: link-inqcust-abends-afct
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70): the LINK to INQCUST abends AFCT (RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACCCU's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes it and the callee never runs

scenarios.name: open-attach-abends-ad2x
scenarios.why: #6271 (X73): OPEN ACC-CURSOR is issued and the CICS-Db2 attach's TCB fails (AD2X): the task abends AD2X, so ABEND-HANDLING takes its none arm (an abend code that is neither AD2Z nor a storm-drain AFC code) and ABENDs it afterwards

notes: CBSA's INQACCCU on GENERATED Db2 rows (#4507): 30 IBMUSER.ACCOUNT rows built from CRETB01's CREATE TABLE and CREI101's index (every column at its boundaries, a NULL in every nullable column; a quarter under sort code 123456), their ACCOUNT_CUSTOMER_NUMBER cycling through customers 1, 2, 4 and 5 (customer.txt holds 1, 2, 4 under 987654, not 5), so ACC-CURSOR meets customers with several, one and no accounts; 30 generated LINKs draw CUSTOMER-NUMBER from those rows (a fifth of the time one the table does not hold). Every task's statements are compared with what Db2 answered (compare_sql), and ACCOUNT after every task. The hand scenarios of cbsa-inqacccu that do not depend on its seed.sql rows (customer 0, 9999999999, 5 not on file, a caller's data left in the COMMAREA) stay. Data: customer.txt is SYNTHETIC (cbsa-updcust's). Burned estate (CBSA). Derived from the CICS Bank Sample Application (CBSA), Copyright IBM Corp. 2023, EPL-2.0: LICENSE is the corpus's own. A customer whose rows include a generated NULL date reaches FETCH -305 and the program's failure path; customer 2's rows hold none, so it is the one that returns accounts.
